Sunderdeep · pass six · docs/renovation

The Renovation

Nine phases for the six things the last pass left wrong or unfinished. The phases cover bodies that shove each other, one-wide corridors, ragged wall tops, bare rooms, a plain chest, the old spell and log icons, and a camp that is a ring of boxes. Every number on this page comes from tools/measure.mjs or the game's own gates. Anything not measured says so.

The plan

order, and why that order
first · the sim1 → 2 → 3

Engagement, then corridor shape, then wall geometry. Phases 4 and 5 stand things against walls, so the walls have to be final before anything is placed.

then · the floor's contents4 → 5

Room dressing and biome chests share one voxel prop pipeline (the D stacker already draws the figures) and one placement rule: against a wall, facing into the room.

then · the screens6 → 7 → 8 → 9

O1 spell icons, O1 loot icons in the log, then the camp. The camp reuses phase 4's props for its stalls and hero plots. Phase 9 re-runs every gate and writes the records.

1

Engagement

item 2 · melee keeps its distance · sim/combat
Cause
Encounter.moveToward steers at the target's centre, and separate() then splits the overlap half and half. A hero closing in, or a third hero looking for room, therefore pushes the enemy it is fighting. Paths also run straight through other bodies.
Measured
A body that is not moving itself is shoved 0.0461 units per engaged second, and the worst single tick is 0.336 (a third of a hex). One test fails: two bodies 0.24 apart.
Change
  • Movement stops at reach − 0.1 rather than at the centre.
  • Melee claims a free hex round its target (an engagement ring), so four heroes spread round one enemy instead of queueing through it.
  • Separation weights by motion: whoever moved this tick gives way, and a planted body (mid-swing, or in reach) is an anchor.
  • A* adds cost for occupied cells.
  • Monster reach is never less than body contact plus 0.15.
Files
sim/combat/Encounter.ts · separation.ts · new engage.ts · dungeon/pathfind/
GateShove below 0.005 per engaged second, worst tick below 0.05. The stacking test passes. Census all in band; simulate median within ±10% of 14.
after: 0.0043 per second · worst 0.034
2

Three-wide corridors

item 3 · sim/dungeon/generate
Cause
corridors.ts digs one hex line through an elbow, and only one corridor in three gets a second cell. A corridor is where most fights end up, so four heroes and a pack meet in single file.
Measured
24.1% of corridor cells sit inside a fully open three-wide band (24 floors). The worst floor has 5%.
Change
  • Every line cell carves its radius-1 hex disc, and elbows carve radius 2 so the turn stays three wide.
  • placeDoors recognises a three-cell mouth where a corridor meets a room and marks its middle cell as the door. The posts go on the mouth's outer edges.
  • paramsForDepth grows the grid by the corridor area it now needs, so rooms don't merge into one hall.
Files
generate/corridors.ts · rooms.ts · Floor.ts (connectivity is still asserted)
Gate100% of corridor cells are in a three-wide band. Every floor is connected. Tests, census and simulate all pass.
after: 100.0% · worst floor 1
3

Watertight wall mass

item 5 · render/tiles/HexMesher
Cause
Only a closed cell that touches the floor gets a top, and each top chooses its own height (stub or full) from its own neighbours. Two adjacent tops can therefore sit at 0.3 and 1.0 with no face between them, and the band stops in void one cell out. The thin runs are separate boxes whose ends don't meet at hex corners.
Measured
Over 8 floors: 403 unfaced height steps and 2584 top edges that end in void.
Change
  • A pure wallMass(grid) gives every closed cell within 2 of the floor a height. A cell is cut to a stub when the floor lies behind it from the camera, decided once per cell by one rule, so the stub band is contiguous.
  • Each massed cell is a hex prism: a capstone top, and a masonry side face on every edge whose neighbour is lower (floor, stub or ground).
  • Beyond the band lies a dark ground plane, never void.
  • The test calls the same function the mesher calls.
Files
new render/tiles/wallMass.ts (pure) · HexMesher.ts · gen/textures/hexSurface.ts (capstone)
Gate0 unfaced steps and 0 void edges, from the same tool. One screenshot per biome, all 8 looked at.
after: 0 steps · 0 void edges
4

Room dressing

item 3 · decorations, torches · data/dressing · gen/sprites/props
What
  • Each room rolls a theme: library, barracks, storeroom, shrine, mess hall, armoury, crypt, or bare.
  • It also rolls a condition: destroyed about 55%, ransacked 35%, intact 10%. That is "sometimes destroyed, rarely intact".
  • Pieces:
    • bookshelf, bed, table, bench, barrel, crate, weapon rack, altar, sarcophagus, banner
    • rubble, bone pile, cobweb
    Each piece comes in intact, broken and wrecked variants.
  • Each biome gets its own torch and light colour:
    • Cisterns: green-glass lantern
    • Ossuary: skull sconce, pale flame
    • Fungal Reach: glow-cap cluster
    • Cinderworks: iron brazier
    • Drowned Vault: teal lantern
    • Rimehollow: cold-blue candle
    • Sable Court: candelabrum, brass-grey
    • Wyrm Deeps: ember bowl
How
  • Placement is sim data (R1). Pieces stand on floor cells against a wall and face into the room.
  • A piece blocks its cell, and the floor's connectivity is re-verified after each one. A piece that would cut a path is dropped.
  • Pieces never go on a door, a stair, a mouth or a spawn cell.
  • Pieces are voxel models sprite-stacked like the D figures. They are cached per piece, state, biome and angle.
Files
new data/dressing/ · sim/dungeon/generate/dress.ts · gen/sprites/props.ts · render/props/Dressing.ts
GateEvery biome dressed, looked at in 8 screenshots. Connectivity is asserted on 200 floors. No piece sits on a door, stair or spawn. Draw calls are counted before and after.

Biome chests

item 3 · chests · gen/sprites/props
What

Eight chests, each drawn open and shut, at about 1.5× today's size:

  • Cisterns: moss-furred oak, iron bands
  • Ossuary: bone reliquary
  • Fungal Reach: root-bound trunk with caps
  • Cinderworks: riveted strongbox with glowing seams
  • Drowned Vault: barnacled sea chest
  • Rimehollow: rime-crusted coffer
  • Sable Court: black lacquer with brass-grey fittings
  • Wyrm Deeps: scaled hoard chest

No gold on any of them.

How
  • Voxel models, rendered at the actor's own angles.
  • The chest spot moves to a floor cell against a wall, with the chest's back to the wall. The facing is stored on the interactable.
  • The O1 chest icon stays for UI use.

6

O1 spell icons

item 1 · gen/art · ui/screens/character

This is the proposal's spell grammar (docs/item-proposals/lib/parts.js · spellIconParts), ported. The rendered sheet is shots/O1-spells.png in that folder. Each icon has:

  • a dark disc
  • an element-hued ring
  • the school frame
  • a sigil hashed from the spell id, so a spell always has the same mark
  • the damage-type mark, bottom left
  • an area pictogram, bottom right

Martial actions get a weapon-stamp variant instead of a sigil.

They replace SCHOOL_ICON and VFX_ICON in Magic, Learn, Queue, the queue editor, the slot picker and the scroll card.

GateAll 80 ActionDefs render without error. No SCHOOL_ICON or VFX_ICON use remains. Screenshots 15-magic, 16-queue and 17-queue-editor looked at.
7

O1 icons in the log

item 4 · ui/log/LogFeed

The loot row in the descent log draws icon(loot.glyph ?? 'g-loot'), a manuscript SVG. It will draw the dropped item's own O1 icon instead:

  • gear from its base and rarity
  • stacks from their stack id

The icon is cached as a data URL. The same audit covers every other place an item still wears a glyph (item card, shop, hoard).

GateA grep audit finds no item glyph path. A descent log screenshot with loot rows is looked at.

The camp, rebuilt

item 6 · sim/dungeon/campLayout · render/scenes/CampScene
Ground
  • A larger camp: the palisade ring goes from 8 to 13 hexes, and the grid grows to match.
  • Paving near the fire, a trodden ring, grass beyond.
  • The palisade becomes sharpened stakes with gaps, not masonry.
Stalls

Six voxel stalls: posts, a cloth awning in the trade's colour, a counter, and wares for each trade:

  • Chronicler: ledgers and a lectern
  • weaponsmith: anvil, rack and whetstone
  • armourer: stand and mail
  • alchemist: shelves of flasks and a still
  • arcanist: a scroll case and a crystal
  • tinkerer: gears and a workbench

The D traders stand behind their counters.

Hero plots

Each party member gets a plot on the outer ring, dressed by background (12 kits, data), for example:

  • soldier: tent and weapon rack
  • acolyte: shrine
  • sage: book stack and desk
  • criminal: crates under a tarp
  • outlander: pelts and a drying rack
  • noble: pavilion and chest
  • entertainer: wagon and drum
  • folk hero: haycart
  • guild artisan: bench
  • haunted one: warding candles
  • charlatan: a trick table
  • urchin: bedroll and scraps
Fire

The heroes stand round the fire in the middle. The fireplace is a stone ring with logs, a spit and pot, and log seats.

Ember motes and warm light are the only motion.

GateCamp screenshots looked at. ui-checks passes. Every stall tap still opens its shop. Every one of the 12 kits is rendered once on a sheet.

Verification & records

every gate again · the handover

npm run verify (typecheck · lint · contrast · headless · test · audits · simulate), npm run census, ui-checks, the full screenshot set, and tools/measure.mjs again to fill the "after" column.

Then the records: 05-code-map.md, the directives (bugs, traps, decisions), a handover and its row, and a CLAUDE.md diff shown for approval. Performance on a phone is not measured unless a device run happens.
